correctness.rationale: Analytic perturbation of the simple Floquet-Perron branch gives p1=Hv, lambda1=0 and the exact lambda2= integral u^T (lambda0 H^2-HMH)v. Left/right eigenvector identities yield the displayed nonnegative directed graph energy, and strong connectivity proves its sharp equality condition. Exact rational test cases reproduce 1/48 and 34/351, and numerical Floquet samples tend to these values. The proof handles piecewise-continuous forcing by analytic Dyson expansion and a.e. integration.

originality.rationale: Inspected the 2024 primary full text including Proposition 1 (N=2 second order) and Proposition 6 (general first-order cancellation), the 2023 full text global conjecture, and the July 2024 full text counterexample discussion. Neither inspected source gives the positive Dirichlet formula for arbitrary multi-phase diagonal modulation on an irreducible nonreversible network. Private indexed-record searches found nonmonotonicity and calendar-reversal findings, but none with the local universal positive graph-energy formula. Publication priority remains uncertain in unindexed literature.
residual_risks: A structurally equivalent general periodic diagonal-modulation theorem may appear in unindexed spectral perturbation or positive-system literature.
The earlier two-environment formula already implies its two-phase specialization; novelty is limited to the general multi-phase network energy and strict equality criterion.
The theorem is local in environmental period; global monotonicity fails in related nonsymmetric systems.

value.rationale: The previously studied high-frequency limit has a vanishing first-order term; the new network Dirichlet law makes the first nonzero term computable and strictly positive without reversibility, revealing precisely when slower-but-rapid forcing boosts growth. This addresses the small-period regime of an asymmetric global monotonicity problem known to admit counterexamples at larger periods, and it applies to any number of environmental phases.
